questions.text: Which of the following is the most appropriate title for the passage?
questions.context: Wildlife management agencies once assumed that a targeted programme to exterminate an invasive predator species would straightforwardly restore the native prey population it had been suppressing. Ecologists who tracked outcomes across several such programmes complicated this assumption considerably: removing the invasive predator sometimes allowed a second, previously suppressed invasive species to expand unchecked instead, since the original predator had inadvertently been controlling that second invader's population as well. Some agencies have since shifted toward modelling an entire local food web before intervening, precisely because removing a single species, however clearly harmful, can restructure an ecosystem in ways a narrower, single-species focus never anticipates.

options.text: Why Removing an Invasive Predator Always Restores the Native Ecosystem
Why Removing One Invasive Species Can Unintentionally Restructure an Entire Ecosystem
A History of Wildlife Management Policy
Why Invasive Species Are Always Easy to Identify
How Ecologists Model Food Webs Using Computer Simulations

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate topic of the passage.
questions.context: A country experiencing significant emigration of skilled workers is often assumed to suffer a straightforward loss that a comparable wave of immigrants arriving from elsewhere could simply offset in economic terms. Labour economists studying these flows in detail complicate this simple offsetting logic: an emigrating engineer and an immigrant arriving with different qualifications are rarely substitutable in the specific sectors each actually affects, meaning a country can experience simultaneous shortages in the sector emigrants left and surpluses in the sector immigrants entered, a mismatch that a simple net migration count entirely conceals.

options.text: the legal process required to gain skilled-worker immigration status
how emigration and immigration in different sectors can create simultaneous shortages and surpluses a simple net count conceals
the total number of skilled workers who emigrate annually worldwide
why some countries restrict skilled worker emigration through policy
a comparison of two specific countries' net migration statistics

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate topic of the passage.
questions.context: A police department that reforms its interrogation procedures to reduce prolonged psychological pressure is sometimes assumed by critics to be making confessions harder to obtain and therefore weakening the department's ability to solve crimes. Departments that have actually implemented such reforms report a more complicated outcome: overall confession rates change little, but the confessions obtained under reformed procedures prove substantially more likely to be corroborated by independent physical evidence later, suggesting the reform did not reduce confessions so much as filter out the unreliable ones prolonged pressure had previously been generating alongside genuine ones.

options.text: the legal standards required for a confession to be admissible in court
how reforming interrogation procedures can filter out unreliable confessions without reducing overall confession rates
the total number of confessions obtained annually under reformed procedures
why some departments have abolished interrogation entirely
a comparison of two specific departments' interrogation policies

questions.text: Which of the following best states the main point of the passage?
questions.context: A weather forecaster who predicts a storm's path days in advance is often judged solely by whether the storm ultimately followed that exact predicted path, a standard that treats any deviation as evidence of poor forecasting. Meteorologists studying forecast accuracy complicate this standard: a forecast expressed as a probability distribution across several plausible paths, rather than a single confident line, can be genuinely excellent even when the storm follows one of several paths the forecast had assigned only moderate likelihood to, since the forecast's honesty about genuine uncertainty is itself a mark of quality, not a failure to predict correctly.

options.text: A forecast should always be judged solely by whether the storm followed its single predicted path exactly.
A forecast's honest expression of genuine uncertainty can itself be a mark of quality, not a failure.
Meteorologists agree that probability-based forecasts are always less accurate than single-path predictions.
A storm always follows the single path a forecast assigns the highest likelihood to.
Forecast accuracy has no meaningful relationship to how uncertainty is expressed.

questions.text: How many of the statements below do NOT agree with the passage?
questions.context:
I spent the first few months after my father's passing convinced I needed to remodel his entire study before I could bring myself to use the room at all, certain that nothing in it could stay exactly as he had left it. It wasn't until a close friend gently pointed out that I had been avoiding the room entirely rather than actually planning any renovation, that I understood the remodelling idea had never been a real plan, only a way of postponing a decision I wasn't ready to make. I eventually changed almost nothing in the room, just cleared a single shelf for my own books, and found I could sit there comfortably within a week of making that much smaller decision. I still keep meaning to thank that friend properly for noticing what I had been avoiding.

Statements
(a) The writer initially believed the study needed a complete remodel before she could use it.
(b) The writer had already begun planning the renovation in detail before her friend spoke up.
(c) A close friend pointed out that the writer had been avoiding the room entirely.
(d) The writer eventually changed almost nothing in the room besides clearing a single shelf.
(e) The writer found she could sit comfortably in the room within a week of the smaller change.
(f) The writer has already properly thanked the friend who made this observation.

questions.text: Which statement does NOT agree with the two explanations given in the passage?
questions.context: Weather agencies that switched from single-path storm predictions to probability-based forecasts report the change was initially unpopular with the public despite being more statistically honest, a resistance two competing explanations attempt to account for. One explanation holds that the public simply finds a single confident prediction easier to plan around, and a probability distribution across several paths demands a kind of interpretive effort most casual forecast readers are unwilling to invest. A second, competing explanation instead proposes that decades of exposure to single-path forecasts had trained the public to expect false certainty, and the probability-based format felt, by comparison, like an admission of incompetence rather than a genuine improvement in honesty.

options.text: The first explanation attributes resistance to the interpretive effort a probability distribution demands.
The first explanation suggests a single confident prediction is simply easier to plan around.
The second explanation claims the public had always expected genuine uncertainty from forecasts.
The second explanation attributes resistance to decades of training toward expecting false certainty.
Both explanations attempt to account for the same initial public resistance to probability-based forecasts.

questions.context: Colonial military garrisons stationed in distant territories relied heavily on veteran soldiers rather than fresh recruits, since veterans had already adapted to unfamiliar climates and diseases that regularly incapacitated newly arrived troops within their first year. Military historians studying garrison mortality records found that units composed primarily of veterans suffered measurably lower non-combat mortality than units composed primarily of fresh recruits stationed in the identical location, a gap attributable almost entirely to accumulated physiological adaptation rather than any difference in combat exposure between the two groups, since both groups faced comparable combat risk overall.
